summary: Mostly no. Crossing a session's previous high or low did the same as random entries on 1h, 4h and daily, for London, New York, weekday and Monday ranges alike. The one result that held: on 4h, entries while price stayed above the previous day's high beat random by 0.50% after 20 candles.

notes: Crosses of a session's previous high did the same as random everywhere they were tested. On 1h, the weekday cross up through the previous day's high came in 0.13% ahead of random, inside a luck band of -0.15% to 0.22%. The Monday-range cross up through Monday's high stayed inside the band on 1h, 4h and daily. The London and New York versions did the same.

The one pooled result above the band comes from the level, not the cross. On 4h, price above the previous day's high enters about four and a half times as often as the cross up through it, and beat random by 0.50% after 20 candles. By pair, ETH sat inside the band, and BTC and SOL each beat random only because of one stretch. In uptrends it came in at 0.51% against a band top of 0.53%, and in downtrends at 0.19%, so neither regime cleared the band on its own.

Buying as price crossed down through the London session's previous low did 0.74% worse than random on 4h. That rests on 2 entries on Apr 10–12, 2024. Without them it is the same as random, though it stays worse at 50 and 100 candles. In downtrends it again looked worse only because of 2 entries on Jun 1–2, 2026, and in uptrends it was the same as random. On 1h the same rule was 0.15% behind random, inside the band.

Some settings split by trend while the pooled result showed nothing. On 4h, the weekday cross up through the previous day's high beat random by 0.66% in uptrends, but only because of 4 entries on Dec 19–22, 2023. In downtrends it was the same as random. On daily, the Monday-range cross up through Monday's high beat random in uptrends only because of entries between Jun 30, 2021 and Sep 7, 2021, and showed nothing in downtrends. On 4h, price above the London previous midpoint did worse than random in downtrends, resting on 5 entries on Nov 10–11, 2022, during the FTX collapse.

On daily, price above the previous day's high had only 28 independent moves, so its 2.61% lead was never judged. That lead comes from one stretch of 80 entries between Dec 14, 2020 and Nov 4, 2021. In uptrends alone it reached 31 moves and beat random only because of entries between Mar 8, 2021 and Nov 4, 2021. In downtrends it showed nothing. The short on a cross down through Monday's low was the same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. Its SOL daily lead rests on entries between Apr 29, 2022 and Sep 13, 2022.

For a long DCA bot, session crosses add no timing on these pairs, so the DCA orders and take profit do the work. If you test one session condition, test price above the previous day's high on 4h as a filter beside your other start conditions. Don't count on it to carry a trend filter, because neither uptrends nor downtrends cleared the band alone. Leave out the London break below the previous low as a dip-buy trigger: on 4h it never did better than random.
